Item 1. Business

The Company designs, manufactures and markets widgets used across many industries. It sells through direct and indirect distribution channels worldwide and operates manufacturing facilities in several countries. Item 1A. Risk Factors

Our business is subject to numerous risks. Demand for our widgets may decline due to macroeconomic conditions, competitive pressure, or changes in customer preferences. We depend on a concentrated set of suppliers for critical components, and supply chain disruption could materially harm our results of operations. We face intense competition in every market we serve, and pricing pressure could compress our margins.

We are exposed to litigation and regulatory risk in multiple jurisdictions, including product liability claims, intellectual property disputes, and evolving data privacy regulation. Failure to comply could result in significant fines and reputational harm. Our indebtedness could limit our operating flexibility, and rising interest rates would increase our financing costs. We may not realize the expected benefits of acquisitions.

Climate-related events could disrupt our facilities and those of our suppliers. We rely on information technology systems that are subject to cyberattack, and a material breach could disrupt operations and expose confidential information, harming our business.

Item 2. Properties

The Company owns and leases facilities worldwide.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Net revenue increased 8% year over year driven by higher unit volume in our premium widget line, partially offset by foreign exchange headwinds. Gross margin expanded 120 basis points reflecting favorable mix and commodity cost declines. Operating expenses grew slower than revenue as we maintained hiring discipline across the organization.

Operating cash flow remained strong and we returned capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. We expect capital expenditures to increase modestly next year to support capacity expansion. Liquidity remains sufficient to fund operations for the foreseeable future, supported by cash on hand and committed credit facilities.
